15:1.sourceText: Ὀφείλομεν δὲ ἡμεῖς οἱ δυνατοὶ τὰ ἀσθενήματα τῶν ἀδυνάτων βαστάζειν, καὶ μὴ ἑαυτοῖς ἀρέσκειν.
15:1.targetText: We who are strong ought to bear with the shortcomings of the weak and not to please ourselves.

groups.note: The article οἱ with the adjective is rendered who.

unmappedSource.reason: The connective δέ is not separately expressed in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula; the Greek has no being verb here.

15:2.sourceText: ἕκαστος ἡμῶν τῷ πλησίον ἀρεσκέτω εἰς τὸ ἀγαθὸν πρὸς οἰκοδομήν·

groups.note: The article τῷ is rendered as the possessive his.
The article τό is rendered as the possessive his.
The noun οἰκοδομήν ("building up") is rendered as a verb.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for build up; the Greek has none.

15:27.sourceText: ηὐδόκησαν γάρ, καὶ ὀφειλέται εἰσὶν αὐτῶν· εἰ γὰρ τοῖς πνευματικοῖς αὐτῶν ἐκοινώνησαν τὰ ἔθνη, ὀφείλουσιν καὶ ἐν τοῖς σαρκικοῖς λειτουργῆσαι αὐτοῖς.
15:27.targetText: They were pleased to do it, and indeed they owe it to them. For if the Gentiles have shared in their spiritual blessings, they are obligated to minister to them with material blessings.

targetPhrases.text: They were pleased to do it

groups.note: The actual being-pleased predicate concerns the just-mentioned contribution; BSB makes its understood action explicit as to do it. No separate Greek doing verb or object pronoun is invented for this English predicate expansion.
The Greek explanatory/affirmative γάρ is rendered as indeed in BSB rather than a second printed for; its discourse force is retained without moving the later actual for particle.
Greek they are debtors is rendered they owe it. The debtors noun and finite copula jointly express the owing predicate, including the English contextual obligation object it.
The Greek genitive their/of them specifies whose debtors they are; English gives the same creditor relation as to them with owe.

Actual dative article and substantival spiritual adjective jointly supply in ... spiritual-blessings as the sharing complement. Blessings is contextual nominal support for spiritual-things, not a separate Greek blessing noun. The intervening their keeps its own actual possessive anchor; no Greek in preposition is invented.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek also accompanies the ministering obligation; BSB does not separately express that additive particle.
The Greek article is not separately expressed with material blessings.
